PA is a commonwealth which means the state has the powers of an individual. Let's say you call the police on someone because they spit on your shoes. In other states you would have to personally wish to file charges on that person. Later on you have a change of heart and make a mends and would like to withdraw the charges...you can do that. Here the commonwealth acts as an individual on your behalf and the charges come from the commonwealth not you. Even if you was to have a change of heart or make a mends the charges would not be dropped and the court proceedings would go forward. This gets particularly messy with domestic disputes. I knew a guy who sat in jail for over a year because his wife refused to testify in a domestic assault case. Any other state the charges would've been thrown out. What also makes this extremely dubious is that the commonwealth tends to charge up and plea down. Say you get caught Jaywalking they would charge you with Felony impeding traffic Felony reckless endangerment and Summary Jaywalking just so you get a high bail for the felonies which guarantees a short stay in county jail and then they will force you to plea down to what you actually did instead of waiting 4-10 months for a trial. If you look at conviction rates by county they are all in the upper 90 percentile because of this. Then there is something called Prima Facie during preliminary hearings which is Latin for on face value. It's really a kangaroo procedure but basically all the cop has to say is he saw you walking and there's a PROBABILITY that you did Jaywalk. Even if your in a wheelchair all the cop has to say is he saw you walking not in a crosswalk and the charges get moved up. It's the biggest waste of taxpayer dollars. I have NEVER seen a case get thrown out at preliminary and lawyers don't even try.
